chunks: From him, from Abdul-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abu Harun al-Makfuf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) would say whenever he mentioned the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'By my father and my mother and my people and my clan! It is strange of the Arabs, how they do not carry us upon their heads.'
And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says in His Book: 'And you were on the brink of a pit of fire, then He saved you from it.'
So it was by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that they were saved.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Quranic verse 3:103 in relation to the Ahl al-Bayt according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) highlights the paradox of Arab ingratitude by citing Quran 3:103, where divine rescue from the 'brink of a fire' is explicitly linked to the Prophet (saw). This narration underscores the Shia theological view that the Ahl al-Bayt, as the living embodiment of the Prophet's message, deserve the highest honor as the means through which the Ummah attained salvation.

en.sarwar: 389. From him, from Abdul Rahmaan Bin Abu Najraan, from Abu Haroun Al-Makfouf, who has narrated the following:

Whenever Abu Abdullah (a.s.) mentioned the Rasool Allah (saww), he would say: ‘By my (a.s.) father (a.s.), and my (a.s.) mother (as), and by my (a.s.) people, and my (a.s.) relatives! It is strange of the Arabs, how they have not carried us (a.s.) upon their heads,
and Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic is Saying in His (azwj) Book: “[3:103] and you were on the brink of a pit of fire, then He saved you from it”,
so it was by the Rasool Allah (saww) that they were saved’.
